title: Return from a recursive level
statement: For any bit string $x$, Boolean values $v,b$, and natural numbers $k,S,B$ with $k+1\le B$ and $2S+1\le B$, the seven-register program with its specified oracle has a run from the return label carrying $v$, at depth $k+1$, stack value $2S+b$, and pointer zero, to depth $k$, stack value $S$, and pointer zero. The final label is $\mathrm{rt}(v)$ if $b$ is true and the first return-copy label carrying $v$ if $b$ is false. Every configuration before the final configuration satisfies the program precondition and has every register value at most $B$.
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string and let $B,k,S$ be natural numbers. For either Boolean values
$v,b$, if $k+1\le B$ and $2S+1\le B$, the fixed seven-register program, with its
specified oracle, can run from the return state carrying $v$, at depth $k+1$ and stack
value $2S+b$, to depth $k$ and stack value $S$. The input pointer and all scratch
registers are zero at both endpoints; throughout the run, every register remains at most
$B$ and every configuration satisfies the program's precondition.
